title: CSS multiple-column layout
learningObjectives: Explain css multiple-column layout and its role in modern CSS.
Write valid CSS syntax and predict the computed result.
Choose the technique appropriate to a real interface requirement.
Identify common implementation, accessibility, and browser-support pitfalls.
Test and explain the behaviour using browser developer tools.

understand.concept: The CSS multi-column module flows content into newspaper-like columns. column-count requests a number of columns; column-width suggests a preferred column width; columns is a shorthand. column-gap controls spacing and column-rule draws a divider. column-span: all allows an element to span across columns in supported layouts. The browser balances content by default in many cases, and fragmentation can split content across columns. Multi-column layout is designed primarily for flowing text, not for building a precise two-dimensional card grid.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing the correct layout model avoids fighting the browser. Multi-column layout is useful for long editorial text, while Grid and Flexbox are usually better for interface components and aligned cards.
understand.analogy: Multi-column layout is like a newspaper page where a long article flows from one column to the next.
understand.analogyLimit: Unlike a newspaper designed by hand, the browser calculates column breaks and may rebalance content as the available width changes.

explain.narrative: Turn a long article into two columns, add a column rule, and make a heading span all columns. Then compare the result with a CSS Grid card layout.

examples.explanation: The article flows through two columns with a gap and divider. On narrow screens, a single column may be more readable.
examples.expectedOutput: Long article text flows into two newspaper-style columns.

examples.explanation: The columns shorthand combines a preferred width and maximum count. The heading spans all columns, after which content continues in the column flow.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser creates columns at least approximately 18rem wide, up to three where space allows.

practise.guidedTask: Apply multi-column layout to a long article. Test column-count and column-width, add a column rule, and make one heading span all columns.
practise.independentTask: Choose between multi-column, Grid, and Flexbox for three layouts: an editorial article, a dashboard of cards, and a navigation bar. Explain why each layout model fits.
hints: Use multi-column for flowing text rather than aligned dashboard cards.
column-width is a preferred width; the available container space affects the final count.
Test reading order and column breaks at narrow viewport widths.

questions.prompt: Which property requests a specific number of columns?
questions.explanation: column-count sets the requested number of columns.

questions.prompt: Which property controls the gap between columns?

options: Allows an element to span across all columns
questions.answer: Allows an element to span across all columns
questions.explanation: column-span can make an element span the full multi-column container.

questions.prompt: Which layout is usually better for a precise dashboard card grid?
questions.explanation: Grid provides explicit two-dimensional track control for aligned cards.

questions.prompt: What is the primary use case for CSS multi-column layout?
options: Flowing long text into newspaper-like columns
questions.answer: Flowing long text into newspaper-like columns
questions.explanation: Multi-column layout is intended for continuous content flow.
